entries.title: Getting Started
entries.body_raw:
#T Getting Started#!
If you are new or returning, the changes can be overwhelming because there are so many.

#T First, Check Your Settings#!
First check if you actually started with the correct settings. You can change a bunch of things you do not like. The game is balanced around the default settings, but I personally often play without Variable Harvests.

#T Recommended Community Mods#!
I personally almost always use the Community Mod Framework mods Faster Universalis, with default settings, and Construction Manager. Construction Manager especially allows you to build or upgrade buildings based on the time they take to pay for their building cost. Since P&P changes building costs in a lot of places, this is a much more sensible metric than building based on profit.

#T What to Pay Attention To#!
In general, this mod makes food much more important. When you urbanize, you increase your food consumption. This food needs to be produced somewhere and distributed.

The most important thing I try to make happen is that expensive food in the food market creates a cascading effect where building up your downstream food production becomes profitable and necessary.

In simple terms, it always works like this:
$BULLET$ 1. Turn the food slider low; do not bankrupt yourself.
$BULLET$ 2. If food is short, rural buildings switch to feeding the province by themselves: farms provision it with their crop. [ShowBuildingTypeName('cookshop')|e] and [ShowBuildingTypeName('public_kitchen')|e] always serve their dishes to the province.
$BULLET$ 3. If [ShowGoodsName('victuals')|e] are cheap, build a [ShowBuildingTypeName('tavern')|e]. It buys victuals from the goods market and feeds the province with them, and it earns more while the province store is low.
$BULLET$ 4. If food is cheap and province storages are full, your population grows faster and you get more prosperity.
$BULLET$ 5. If food is expensive, your population grows slower and you get less prosperity.

It is best to understand how [ShowBuildingTypeName('tavern')|e] works. It hires and fires people based on whether buying victuals for the province pays off, which is the case while the province store is low. You can subsidize it, but you rarely need to. Just leave it be and build it in cities where you do not want to produce food with [ShowBuildingTypeName('cookshop')|e]. Its counterpart [ShowBuildingTypeName('victualling_yard')|e] packs a full province store into victuals for the goods market; it belongs where rivers, coasts and market centres let the victuals travel.

Essentially everything is balanced around this idea.

#T RGOs#!
RGOs are removed and replaced by buildings. Buildings are just more interesting.

#T Variable Harvests#!
They happen yearly and make your crop production vary a lot.

#T Map Modes#!
Please familiarize yourself with the map modes. I added a lot. They are very helpful for many things.

#T Farming, Forest, and Fishing Capacity#!
There are map modes for these as well. They are just shared buckets for buildings. For example, building a farming building removes one capacity point from the farming capacity bucket. The idea is that buildings that use arable land compete for space.

#T Land Attributes#!
This is a static modifier produced by a complicated out-of-game pipeline. It calculates the fertility of a location based on many out-of-game factors that do not exist in game, like soil, water access, temperatures, and more.

#T Building Levels#!
You will see some locations cannot build too many buildings until they reach their capacity. You can still overbuild, but it would be wise to build infrastructure buildings so you do not suffer the consequences of being over capacity.

Please use the filters in the building menu or the relevant map mode to find the places where you are over capacity and build the buildings there.

#T Internal Food Goods#!
[ShowGoodsName('province_food_sales')|e] pays the [ShowBuildingTypeName('grange')|e] for the surplus of a well-stocked province, and nothing once the store runs low. It is an internal good that lets the Grange react to the province store by itself. You can otherwise ignore it.

entries.title: F.A.Q.
entries.body_raw:
#T Q: Are my other mods compatible with Prosper or Perish?:#!
I recommend playing with the Community Framework mods Faster Universalis and Construction Manager. For everything else, you need to try it yourself or ask in the Discord. If you test other mods, load Prosper or Perish last and run an Observer test before committing to a campaign.

#T Q: An update ruined my save. What do I do?:#!
Steam Workshop updates can break old saves. Download the matching older release from https://github.com/JanB1989/prosper-or-perish-constructor/releases . Extract the repository archive, open its mod folder, and copy the Prosper or Perish (Population Growth & Food Rework) folder into C:\Users\YourUserName\Documents\Paradox Interactive\Europa Universalis V\mod . Then use that local copy for the old save instead of the auto-updating Workshop copy.

#T Q: How do I install the GitHub version?:#!
Go to https://github.com/JanB1989/prosper-or-perish-constructor and download the repository, or download the branch or release you want. Extract it, open the repository's mod folder, and copy the Prosper or Perish (Population Growth & Food Rework) folder into C:\Users\YourUserName\Documents\Paradox Interactive\Europa Universalis V\mod . Then enable that local copy in the EU5 launcher.

#T Q: Why is everyone starving at game start?:#!
I put a lot of effort into cleaning up the start, but the economy can still take a couple of years to settle. I will keep working on this; you are good to go.

entries.title: Update 0.9
entries.body_raw:
#T Update 0.9#!
Hey guys,

Read the Overview page to see roughly what changed. Most should be familiar.

I spent a bunch of time resolving many, many bugs and improving UI clarity. I streamlined many things as well. All of this improved performance and AI performance by a good chunk.

Of course, I added new buildings, new production methods, new advances, and more.

#T Biggest Changes from 0.8#!
$BULLET$ #Y 1. The location building cost malus is gone.#! It is replaced with scaling building cost per industry and the new logistics system, where each location has an inherent building limit depending on many factors like vegetation, topography, and more. This is meant as the rough natural limit of how easily a location can be supplied. If you go over the building limits, you get some negative modifiers. Different buildings allow you to increase the limit. If you are on a big river, for example, the buildings you build are much cheaper to maintain. If you are in a landlocked jungle, you have fewer options and it is more expensive.

$BULLET$ #Y 2. Victuals Markets and Province Food Market Goods.#! It is a constant struggle to make food prices cascade down into making farming buildings possible. I wrote a post about this on the Paradox forum with recommended changes in the thread "Food feedback". This is why I changed the Victuals Market again, as its responsibility is ultimately to convert food goods into local food and allow this cascading effect to happen. The Victuals Market now uses two internal goods: Province Food Sales for food sold into the goods market and Province Food Purchase for food bought back into a province. They serve no purpose other than to create the local conditions where converting victuals to food can be profitable when victuals are cheap and market food is expensive. The AI now perfectly understands this and builds these without any scripting help. I hope in the medium-term future Paradox changes the food system so we do not need all these mechanisms for the food system to function like it should. They are aware of it, and it sounds to me like a medium-term refactor might be in the cards. We have to see and hope.

$BULLET$ #Y 3. Please use the Community Mod Framework.#! I recommend using Faster Universalis as well, and at least use the Construction Manager mod. It allows you to expand buildings based on the time it would take them to pay for themselves. Since we are using increased and decreased building costs in many places, this is the metric you need to expand your buildings most of the time. Monthly profit is much less helpful.

$BULLET$ #Y 4. Bigger and more urbanized cities.#! In general, you will see much bigger and more urbanized cities from the player and the AI. These will have very specialized industries that are very efficient. So, more specialized cities, but expanding these specialized industries will become increasingly expensive. That is very manageable, and it is also multiplicative with the building cost decreases that exist from societal values, etc.

$BULLET$ #Y 5. Promotions.#! I massively reduced the amount of promotions that happen more or less passively. This is the first step toward a kind of education system that will allow for more specialization. Especially burghers are now much harder to come by, so some promotion modifiers might now be worth it. I also buffed libraries and universities, and I allow libraries to be built in rural locations as well.

Otherwise, I hope you enjoy the changes. As usual, everything has been tested a lot, and I know it works with the AI and produces good historical outcomes.

If you have questions, join the Discord; the link is on the Steam mod page. If you find bugs, you can report them there.

I hope you enjoy.

entries.title: Prosper or Perish (Mod)
entries.body_raw:
#T The Mod:#!
This mod overhauls the food system until it is fundamentally different from vanilla. After hundreds of modifier and advance changes and many hours of balancing, food is now the primary driver of pop growth and migration—replacing the old ties to [pp_prosperity|e], Development and similar factors, which instead now shape food capacity and growth.

You will see a sharp split between rural farming locations urbanized rich cities, incentives for local manufacturing in provinces to ease capital-centric "clumping," and higher infrastructure costs so Roads become a strategic choice rather than something to spam.

The core loop is simple: full province and low food prices mean strong growth and many other benefits; empty storages and high prices mean heavy emigration, pop demotion, death and other bad outcomes.

The mod adds new Buildings, new production methods and two new food goods (see [pp_victuals|e]). When you create a new game, check the game rules for Prosper or Perish: you can disable [pp_variable_harvests|e] if you want a steadier food economy without yearly harvest swings. You can also make the campaign harder—higher player building upkeep, stronger AI food efficiency, or cheaper AI building upkeep—or leave everything on defaults for the standard mod experience.

Please read at least [pp_food|e] and [pp_food_consumption|e]; they should be enough to get you playing.

#T Promotions:#!
I massively reduced the amount of promotions that happen more or less passively. This is the first step toward a kind of education system that will allow for more specialization. Especially burghers are now much harder to come by, so some promotion modifiers might now be worth it. I also buffed libraries and universities, and I allow libraries to be built in rural locations as well.

#T Feedback:#!
I really need feedback for specific regions—send it on Steam as a PM or in the mod comments. If some regions look weird or super ahistoric, show me where and I will try to fix it. Same with Cookshop recipes: we may need to add more to represent some regions. Please confirm it is not caused by other mods before sending screenshots.

There are many other changes not covered here. If something is confusing or I forgot to document it, tell me and I will try to add it to this Europedia in the future.

#T How I Add Features:#!
I follow this checklist:

$BULLET$ Is the mechanic fun to manage for the player?
$BULLET$ Is the mechanic a concept that can be understood historically?
$BULLET$ Is the AI able to handle the mechanic?

I am fine with victuals not exactly representing how food was traded and produced historically. I am fine with numbers in-game for how much food a noble consumes or a peasant—these are abstractions to get the game working. I can imagine a noble eating very expensive food, which is the abstraction for why he needs "more" food. But if I cannot even imagine how it would make sense in our world, I will likely only add it to get the game working at all.

#T Thanks:#!
A sincere thank you to everyone who reported bugs, helped with balancing, and took the time to share feedback. Thank you as well to everyone who created compatibility patches and collections around Prosper or Perish, and to the EU5 Mod Coop Discord for the discussions, help, and support.

A special thank you to Karkento for letting me spam him with ideas nonstop and for helping so much with balancing and ideas.

Thanks as well to Noslon for providing valuable feedback and good solutions to fix the employment system.

And a special thank you to Regal Urangutan for creating the EU5 2.0 collection centered around P&P, and for always being ready to chat and excited to talk about EU5.

entries.body_html:
The Mod:

This mod overhauls the food system until it is fundamentally different from vanilla. After hundreds of modifier and advance changes and many hours of balancing, food is now the primary driver of pop growth and migration—replacing the old ties to P&P: Prosperity, Development and similar factors, which instead now shape food capacity and growth.

You will see a sharp split between rural farming locations urbanized rich cities, incentives for local manufacturing in provinces to ease capital-centric "clumping," and higher infrastructure costs so Roads become a strategic choice rather than something to spam.

The core loop is simple: full province and low food prices mean strong growth and many other benefits; empty storages and high prices mean heavy emigration, pop demotion, death and other bad outcomes.

The mod adds new Buildings, new production methods and two new food goods (see P&P: Food Goods). When you create a new game, check the game rules for Prosper or Perish: you can disable P&P: Variable Harvests if you want a steadier food economy without yearly harvest swings. You can also make the campaign harder—higher player building upkeep, stronger AI food efficiency, or cheaper AI building upkeep—or leave everything on defaults for the standard mod experience.

Please read at least P&P: Food Production and P&P: Food Consumption; they should be enough to get you playing.

Promotions:

I massively reduced the amount of promotions that happen more or less passively. This is the first step toward a kind of education system that will allow for more specialization. Especially burghers are now much harder to come by, so some promotion modifiers might now be worth it. I also buffed libraries and universities, and I allow libraries to be built in rural locations as well.

Feedback:

I really need feedback for specific regions—send it on Steam as a PM or in the mod comments. If some regions look weird or super ahistoric, show me where and I will try to fix it. Same with Cookshop recipes: we may need to add more to represent some regions. Please confirm it is not caused by other mods before sending screenshots.

There are many other changes not covered here. If something is confusing or I forgot to document it, tell me and I will try to add it to this Europedia in the future.

How I Add Features:

I follow this checklist:

  • Is the mechanic fun to manage for the player?
  • Is the mechanic a concept that can be understood historically?
  • Is the AI able to handle the mechanic?

I am fine with victuals not exactly representing how food was traded and produced historically. I am fine with numbers in-game for how much food a noble consumes or a peasant—these are abstractions to get the game working. I can imagine a noble eating very expensive food, which is the abstraction for why he needs "more" food. entries.body_raw:
There is no food market. Everything hinges on the province store: food exists only as [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e] in a [province|e]'s store or as a trade good on the goods market.

#T Everything Hinges on the Province Store#!

#T Store Running Low#!

Farms, herds and fisheries make more [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e] for their own province and send fewer [pp_staple_foods|e] to the goods market.

#T Store Full#!

They send more [pp_staple_foods|e] to the goods market and make less Province Food.

Every producer of staple foods splits its output between its province and the market, and the province store decides the split. The store is counted in months of food: a full store makes the province grow, an empty one starves it (see [pp_food_storage|e]).

#T Food Lives in Two Places#!

#T In the Province Store#!

As [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e]. It feeds the [pops|e] of its own province and is never traded: it never leaves the province.

#T On the Goods Market#!

As a trade good: [pp_staple_foods|e] and [ShowGoodsName('victuals')|e] are bought and sold like cloth or iron. On the market they feed nobody until a building turns them into Province Food.

#T Staple Foods#!
hover each good

#T How Food Gets Into the Store#!

#T Subsistence#!

Unemployed [ShowPopTypeName('peasants')] grow their own food. What they do not eat goes into the store.

Farms such as the [ShowBuildingTypeName('wheat_farm')|e], the [ShowBuildingTypeName('cookshop')|e] and the [ShowBuildingTypeName('tavern')|e] make Province Food for their province. See [pp_food|e] for each of them.

entries.title: P&P: Food Production
entries.body_raw:
Food gets into a province store in two ways: through subsistence, when unemployed peasants grow more than they eat, and through buildings that turn [pp_staple_foods|e] or [ShowGoodsName('victuals')|e] into [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e]. Two buildings pack food into victuals for the market instead.

#T Subsistence#!

#T Grows#!

Every unemployed peasant family works its own plot and grows food.

#T Eats#!

The family eats part of it. How much is its [ShowModifierTypeName('global_peasants_food_consumption')].

#T Surplus#!

The rest goes into the province store as [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e].

#T Less Eaten, More Surplus#!

Everything that lowers peasant food consumption raises the surplus: the [ShowBuildingTypeName('cookshop')|e], [Concept('good_harvest', 'strong harvests')|e], [Concept('pp_abundant_free_land', 'Abundant Arable Land')|e] and more.

#T More Eaten, Less Surplus#!

Everything that raises it lowers the surplus: [Concept('poor_harvest', 'weak harvests')|e], [Concept('pp_overused_arable_land', 'Overused Arable Land')|e] and more.

#T Buildings#!

#T Staple Food Farms#!

The [ShowBuildingTypeName('wheat_farm')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('rice_farm')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('cattle_farm')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('fishing_village')|e] and every other building that produces [pp_staple_foods|e] always does both: it feeds its own province with [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e] and sells its crop on the goods market. While the province store runs low it makes more Province Food and sells less; while the store is full it sells more.

#T Cookshops#!

A [ShowBuildingTypeName('cookshop')|e] stands in a town or the province capital and needs farms in its province: the more farms, the more levels it can have. Cookshops and their upgrade, the [ShowBuildingTypeName('public_kitchen')|e], are strong food makers, and they even lower peasant food consumption: fresh food that would spoil is eaten where it is cooked.

#T Granges#!

The [ShowBuildingTypeName('grange')|e] is a building of the [ShowPopTypeName('nobles')] in the province capital. Once the province store is full, it takes the surplus [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e] and sells it as [ShowGoodsName('victuals')|e] on the goods market: less food for the province, more victuals for the market.

#T Victualling Yards#!

The main source of [ShowGoodsName('victuals')|e]. A [ShowBuildingTypeName('victualling_yard')|e] stands in market centres and good harbours, buys [pp_staple_foods|e] on the goods market and packs them into victuals for the market. It never touches the province store.

#T Taverns#!

A [ShowBuildingTypeName('tavern')|e] in the province capital buys [ShowGoodsName('victuals')|e] on the goods market and serves them as [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e]. It is the main way to feed provinces that grow little food, or whose people you would rather put to other work.

entries.title: P&P: Food Consumption
entries.body_raw:
There are many ways to reduce peasant food consumption (they are more focused on subsistence), which directly increases how much food they contribute to the market. It might be worth it for population-rich rural countries to use these modifiers to your advantage. They are not very useful for already highly urbanized countries, who should rather build their own food industry or just buy it from the market.

Food consumption varies with many factors. When food is cheap, people consume more—less rationing, choosier diets. When food is expensive, they consume less: more frugal, more focused on survival. Because of this link to well-being, food consumption modifiers are strong and have wide effects.

#T What Impacts Food Consumption:#!
Several factors change how much pops consume:

$BULLET$ Local food price on the market (cheap vs expensive)
$BULLET$ [pp_province_current_food_storage|e] (growing vs shrinking)
$BULLET$ [pp_prosperity|e] of the location
$BULLET$ Winter severity
$BULLET$ [pp_devastation|e] and recovery conditions
$BULLET$ Pop type (nobles, clergy, burghers, laborers, peasants, soldiers each have different base consumption)

See [pp_food_storage|e] for how storage works.

#T Cheap food in the market and High food Storages in Provinces:#!
When food is cheap on the market and province storages are well stocked, locations receive [pp_cheap_food|e] and provinces with growing storage receive [pp_province_current_food_storage|e]. Effects scale by how far below the base price the food price is.

#T Display Note:#!
Because of Paradox scaling, the maximum value you can actually get is only half of the value shown below.

[ShowModifierEffect('cheap_food_in_location')]

#T Expensive food in the market and Low food Storages in Provinces:#!
When food is expensive on the market and province storages are low or empty, locations receive [pp_expensive_food|e]. People consume less—they get more out of their food, are less picky, and minds focus on feeding families. Other priorities fall by the wayside. Effects scale by how far above the base price the food price is.

#T Display Note:#!
Because of Paradox scaling, the maximum value you can actually get is only half of the value shown below.

[ShowModifierEffect('expensive_food_in_location')]

Food consumption modifiers are deliberately strong because consumption is tightly linked to living standards, labor quality, and social stability. [pp_prosperity|e] reinforces the loop: high food availability boosts prosperity, and prosperity in turn supports higher consumption and [population_growth|e].

#T When You Run Out of food:#!
When storages are empty, a province receives [ShowModifier('province_starving')]. People try to feed themselves by any means necessary. [pp_devastation|e] tends to rise, pops demote to lower classes that consume less, and people starve. Supply limit drops, migration attraction plummets, life expectancy falls, and people flee. [pp_prosperity|e] crashes. Soldiers are less willing to defend [starving|e] cities. See [pp_food_storage|e] and [pp_starvation|e].

[ShowModifierEffect('province_starving')]

#T Devastation:#!
[pp_devastation|e] is best avoided and is caused by starvation or other horrible conditions (blockades, sieges, etc.). For full modifier details and the inversion note (devastation scales 0 to -100%).

[ShowModifierEffect('devastation')]

Packing loses some of the food, so victuals that go out and come back always return less than they took.

Internal Food Goods

Province Food Sales pays the Grange for the surplus of a well-stocked province, and nothing once the store runs low. It is an internal good that lets the Grange react to the province store by itself. You can otherwise ignore it.

#T P&P Buildings#!
Prosper or Perish adds and rewrites many buildings. The exact inputs, outputs, unlocks, and modifiers are shown in the building and production-method tooltips; this page is only orientation.

#T Food Buildings:#!
Farms, fisheries, orchards, and other calorie buildings have a Provisioning slot: they feed their own province with their crop as [ShowGoodsName('local_food')|e], more while the province store is low and less while it is full. #T Non-Farming Raw Goods:#!

entries.title: Building Limits
entries.body_raw:
#T Building Limits#!
Every location has a number of building levels it can supply easily, depending on vegetation, topography, rivers, coasts, roads, rank, development and more.

You can still overbuild. Every level above that number gives the location [ShowModifier('unsupported_building_levels')]: its goods reach the market worse, so its [market_access|e] drops. Use the Unsupported Building Levels map mode to find the places that need help.

#T Logistics Buildings#!
Logistics buildings carry a place's goods to its market. Each level raises [market_access|e] and pays its workers a steady wage in [ShowGoodsName('logistics')]; in exchange a little output of heavy goods such as stone, ores, salt and timber is lost to the haulage. They can only be built where market access is still poor and enough buildings already stand to need them. Build the one that fits the place:

$BULLET$ [ShowBuildingTypeName('river_boatmen_yard')|e] on rivers. Big rivers take more of them.
$BULLET$ [ShowBuildingTypeName('coastal_shipping_office')|e] in ports. Natural harbors take more of them.
$BULLET$ [ShowBuildingTypeName('transport_office')|e] in cities and developed towns.
$BULLET$ [ShowBuildingTypeName('carrier_inn')|e] in rural settlements and towns with roads.
$BULLET$ Where the land has its own carriers, they take the carrier inn's place: the [ShowBuildingTypeName('pp_caravanserai')|e] in the dry lands from the Maghreb to Central Asia, the [ShowBuildingTypeName('pp_oasis_caravan_station')|e] in the Sahara and the Sahel, the [ShowBuildingTypeName('pp_yam_station')|e] from Russia to Mongolia, the [ShowBuildingTypeName('pp_banjara_tanda')|e] in South Asia and the [ShowBuildingTypeName('pp_llama_caravan_post')|e] in the Andes. They need no road.

Big rivers, ports and cities are easy to supply. Landlocked jungle is not. If a place is red on the map mode, build logistics there before you keep stacking industry.

entries.title: P&P: Farming/Fishing/Forest Capacities
entries.body_raw:
Farming, Fishing, and Forest Capacities are about how many rural raw-material building levels a location can sustain, not how much each building produces. For productivity, see [pp_farm_output|e]. Exact current values are shown in the relevant building and map-mode tooltips.

The Farming Capacity, Fishing Capacity, and Forest Capacity map modes are in the Geography map-mode group.

#T Farming Capacity:#!
This pool governs the crop farms such as [ShowBuildingTypeName('wheat_farm')|e] and [ShowBuildingTypeName('wheat_model_farm')|e], orchards, animal farms, plantations, groves, gardens, sericulture farms, simplers groves, and vineyard estates.

Farming Capacity is one current sum. Local farming suitability, matching agricultural RGOs, Maximum RGO Size, [population_capacity|e], location rank, river size, Manorial Customals, irrigation and water-control buildings, existing farming-capacity buildings, and building levels in the location can all add or subtract from it.

#T Fishing Capacity:#!
This pool governs [ShowBuildingTypeName('fishing_village')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('net_curing_yard')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('ocean_fishery')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('drift_net_fishery')|e], and [ShowBuildingTypeName('offshore_fishery')|e]. It does not govern [ShowBuildingTypeName('pearl_fishery')|e].

Fishing Capacity is one current sum. Coasts, lakes, wetlands, fish RGOs, Maximum RGO Size, river size, Manorial Customals, and existing fish-producing buildings can all add or subtract from it.

#T Forest Capacity:#!
This pool governs [ShowBuildingTypeName('forest_village')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('managed_forest_village')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('lumber_mill')|e], [ShowBuildingTypeName('water_sawmill')|e], and [ShowBuildingTypeName('lumber_mill_improved')|e].

Forest Capacity is one current sum. Forest geography, relevant RGOs, Maximum RGO Size, location rank, Manorial Customals, existing forest and lumber buildings, and building levels in the location can all add or subtract from it.

The building maximum-level tooltip and the matching capacity map mode show the same current value. The maximum-level tooltip lists the active sources that add or subtract capacity.

#T Other Raw Material Buildings:#!
Other raw material producing buildings, such as mines, quarries, saltworks, pearl fisheries, charcoal makers, ivory hunting camps, and similar buildings, do not use the three shared pools above. Their maximum level is governed by Rural Building Capacity.

Rural Building Capacity is a simpler cap influenced by the location's basic rural allowance, development, Maximum RGO Size, and river access.

#T Building order:#!
If a building type ends up well above its available capacity, the system can trim excess rural building levels over time. There is no lasting benefit to building around the limit.

entries.title: P&P: Building Output
entries.body_raw:
This entry is about how much rural raw-material buildings produce—their productivity—not how many you can build. For quantity, see [pp_farm_capacity|e].

Over Europa Universalis 5's timeframe, rural productivity rose sharply. The mod reflects this by replacing vanilla's flat food modifier with per-good output modifiers. Each raw material can now gain or lose output independently.

Building Output is affected by both inert and dynamic factors. Any of these can be beneficial or detrimental.

#T Component one:#!
Dynamic factors that change over the game. Some regions or countries may gain access to productivity improvements earlier or later than others:

$BULLET$ Advances
$BULLET$ Societal choices
$BULLET$ Development
$BULLET$ Government reforms
$BULLET$ [ShowBuildingTypeName('irrigation_systems')|e]

#T Component two:#!
Inert factors tied to geography and location. Every location has a unique set of local output modifiers estimated from historical and geographic evidence:

$BULLET$ Rainfall and water availability
$BULLET$ Soil quality
$BULLET$ Climate
$BULLET$ Topography
$BULLET$ Vegetation
$BULLET$ The location's RGO

#T Harvest:#!
Yearly harvest outcomes vary by region and can further boost or reduce agricultural output beyond the factors above. For full details on harvest levels and how they affect food production, see [pp_variable_harvests|e].

entries.title: P&P: Variable Harvests
entries.body_raw:
Every September each [region|e] learns what its fields will give for the year ahead. Most years are ordinary. A bad one shrinks the crops and the surplus of the villages; a good one does the opposite. Neighbouring regions tend to share their luck, and lean or fat years can come in runs.

#T A Harvest Year#!

#T Every September#!

The harvest is settled once a year, for every [region|e] at the same time, and holds until the next September.

#T Broad Harvest Area#!

The map is split into broad areas such as Western Europe or South Asia. Each first draws its season: kind, ordinary or harsh.

#T Each Region#!

Every [region|e] of the area then draws its own harvest. The season tilts the odds, and so does the region's last harvest.

#T Harvest Modifier#!

The harvest lands on every [location|e] of the region as a [location_modifier|e] named after its area. An average year adds none.

#T Lean Years and Fat Years#!

[abysmal_harvest|e] · [very_poor_harvest|e] · [poor_harvest|e] · [average_harvest|e] · [good_harvest|e] · [very_good_harvest|e] · [bountiful_harvest|e]

Hover a harvest to see its modifier in every broad harvest area, then hover an area for the exact effects. Average is the most common harvest and the ends of the scale are the rarest. Each region leans toward its own last harvest: a harsh season after a bad year makes another bad year likelier still, while a harsh season after a good year only brings the odds back to ordinary. Kind seasons work the same way in the other direction.

#T What a Harvest Changes#!

A harvest moves two things in its locations: how much the fields yield and how much surplus the villages have to spare. Each crop swings by how sensitive it is and by how widely its broad area grows it: where it is a main crop it swings at full strength, where it is grown only here and there it swings less. Hover a good for its name.

#T Grain and rice#!
swing the most

#T Field, orchard and plantation crops#!
swing less

#T Hardy goods#!
barely move

#T Herds, flocks, fish and game#!
are spared

The [ShowPopTypeName('peasants')] live off their own plots first. A bad year leaves those plots less surplus for the province, a good year more; the harvest modifier shows this as peasant food consumption. A bad harvest therefore strikes twice: smaller crops and less to spare from the villages.

#T Where to See It#!

$BULLET$ #T The map:#! the Variable Harvests [situation|e] colours every location by this year's harvest, dark for bad years and bright for good ones, and stripes starving provinces.
$BULLET$ #T The location view:#! the harvest chip at the top right shows the location's harvest as the medallions above; hover it for every effect.
$BULLET$ #T The modifier:#! the harvest modifier in the location's modifier list names its broad area and lists its effects.
$BULLET$ #T The game rule:#! Variable Harvests can be switched off when a campaign starts.

entries.title: P&P: Arable Land
entries.body_raw:
Arable Land is what a location's fields, pastures and waters can feed, counted in people rather than acres. Its people live on it, farms take their share of it, and land improvements win more of it. What matters is how full it is: free land lets a location thrive, crowded land holds it back.

#T Where Arable Land Comes From#!

#T The Land Itself#!

[climate|e], [vegetation|e], [topography|e], soil, fertility, rivers and coasts decide what the land can feed. Fertile river valleys feed many, deserts and mountains few.

#T Land Improvements#!

Clearing, draining, irrigating and terracing win new land. How far a location can be improved depends on its geography and grows with its [development|e].

#T Work in Town#!

Whoever works in a [building|e] no longer works a plot of their own, so each building gives back part of its workers' land: workshops and town quarters much, mines and forts little.

#T What Uses It#!

#T People#!

Every [pop|e] lives on the land, townsfolk as much as peasants. A growing town fills its land quickly unless its buildings give land back.

#T Farms#!

Each farm level takes a fixed share of land, larger farms a larger share. A location holds only as many farms as its land has room for, and a little always stays untouched. Farms do not wait for people to leave: built on crowded land, they crowd it further.

#T Reserved Grounds#!

Hunting grounds, royal forests and gardens, great enclosures and cattle pens keep land for their owners and away from the people.

Hover a state for its effects. Nearly empty land gives the strongest bonus: settlers pick the best ground and live partly off what they gather. As people arrive the bonus fades with the land that is left: rural goods yield less extra, the villages have less to spare and fewer newcomers are drawn in. Tribes grow only while land is free. At exactly full nothing applies; past full the land is overused, and that weighs heavier the further people outnumber the land.

$BULLET$ #T The map:#! the arable land map mode in the Population group colours every location by its land.

entries.title: Population Growth
entries.body_raw:
In general, abundance of food causes [population_growth|e]. Positive [population_growth|e] comes from two main sources: [pp_cheap_food|e] and [pp_province_current_food_storage|e].

Negative [population_growth|e] comes from [pp_starvation|e], [pp_expensive_food|e], or low food storages in provinces.

#T Balancing Modifiers:#!
Some modifiers—such as negative [population_growth|e] in cities, towns, and rural locations—exist purely to balance out the positive modifiers and create an equilibrium. They have no other meaning.

#T Arable Land:#!
Growth does not stop at the [population_capacity|e]. Past it the land is [Concept('pp_overused_arable_land', 'Overused Arable Land')|e]: the villages have less to spare and people move away.

entries.title: P&P: Available Arable Land
entries.body_raw:
Part of a location's [population_capacity|e] is still free: [ShowModifier('available_free_land')]. With fewer people competing for the same land, they can choose better fields, pastures, fishing spots and forest work sites instead of being forced onto marginal ground. The effects shrink as the land fills and are gone when it is full; past full the land becomes [Concept('pp_overused_arable_land', 'Overused Arable Land')|e].
